# Olaf Dsouza

> Personal site and engineering blog for Olaf Dsouza, a software engineer focused on operating systems, LLMs, and distributed systems.

Olaf is a software engineer at Netflix and a University of Michigan CS/CSE alum who has also worked at August Law and Quail AI. This site hosts his portfolio, experience, and blog.

## Primary Pages
- [Home](https://olafdsouza.com/): Portfolio, experience, and project overview.
- [Blog](https://olafdsouza.com/blog): Writing on operating systems, LLMs, distributed systems, and CS coursework.
- [Food](https://olafdsouza.com/food): Ranked guides to the 341+ restaurants, coffee shops, bakeries and bars Olaf has rated, with notes and photos.
- [Connections](https://olafdsouza.com/connections): NYT Connections tracking board.

## Blog Posts
- [Your inference provider sucks (at caching)](https://olafdsouza.com/blog/your-inference-provider-sucks-at-caching): The same agent session cost $0.13 on one DeepSeek V4 Flash provider and $2.30 on another. Prompt cache hit rate, not list price, explains the 17.7× gap.
- [The Area Over the Curve](https://olafdsouza.com/blog/the-area-over-the-curve): Why the cheapest LLM is rarely the cheapest result, and how August routes each agent task to just enough model intelligence.
- [Everything is a Workflow](https://olafdsouza.com/blog/everything-is-a-workflow): How workflows became August's abstraction for reliable legal AI agents, growing from saved prompts into a small programming language.
- [HOPS](https://olafdsouza.com/blog/hops-pipeline-simulator): A discrete-event simulator for pipeline-parallel LLM training on heterogeneous GPUs, validated within 2% of real hardware.
- [Frame Classification in Congressional Speeches with NLP](https://olafdsouza.com/blog/nlp-project): Using NLP to classify rhetorical framing in U.S. Congressional speeches, our University of Michigan CSE 595 final project.
- [An Honest Review of Every ULCS Class I Have Taken at Michigan](https://olafdsouza.com/blog/ulcs-class-reviews-michigan): Honest reviews and ratings for every upper-level CS (ULCS) class at the University of Michigan.
